children: Third-quarter industrial earnings reports are right around the corner, giving investors a chance to check trends and firm up their stock-picking convictions heading into 2027.

Citi analyst Andrew Kaplowitz, however, sees an opportunity to add some names ahead of earnings. He sees six names, including data center infrastructure provider Vertiv, reacting positively to reports.

"We remain largely constructive on [industrials] ahead of 3Q earnings as a combination of durable secular tailwinds led by data center-related infrastructure investment and likely still improving/broadening short-cycle demand we think should support solid topline momentum and durable earnings expectations," he wrote in an earnings preview report.

Short-cycle refers to industrial products that don't require much lead time and react quickly to improving conditions. A rivet in a Boeing jet is a short-cycle product. The jet is a long-cycle product, ordered years in advance.

"We are also attuned to risk factors such as potential price versus cost headwinds given persistent inflationary pressures; a higher-for-longer interest rate environment and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, including the potential for policy changes post-election if one or both chambers of Congress [to] flip," Kaplowitz added.

He prefers stocks with higher visibility into continued sales and earnings growth, as well as stocks with good growth that isn't yet reflected in stock prices. The six he likes ahead of earnings are: Vertiv, aerospace and industrial parts supplier Parker-Hannifin, automation technology provider Emerson Electric, cooling solutions company Trane Technologies, diversified manufacturer Dover, and electrical equipment supplier Eaton.
On Oct. 22, Dover will be the first of the group to report earnings.

Parker's guidance is conservative, says Kaplowitz. Data center demand is getting strong, benefiting Vertiv and Eaton. Emerson should see improving profitability, and order growth is expected at Trane. Dover stock is "too cheap."

Dover trades for 17 times estimated 2026 earnings, a discount to the other five, which trade for an average of 30 times. Dover is expected to grow earnings by about 12% a year for the coming three years. That's similar to market growth, but the S&P 500 trades for about 19 times earnings.

Kaplowitz rates all six stocks Buy. His Dover price target is $266. Dover stock was recently at $192. His Parker target is $1,234. Parker stock was just below $967 early on Monday. His Vertiv target is $358, up from current levels of about $240. His Trane price target is $566. Trane stock recently traded at just under $479. His Emerson and Eaton targets are $182 and $498, respectively. Emerson stock was recently $163. Eaton shares were $432.
All six stocks have above-average Buy-rating ratios. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges between 55% and 60%.
Coming into Monday trading, the six were up about 23% year to date. Only Dover stock was down by 3%. Vertiv stock was the top performer, up about 50%.
